It is (arguably) the best fighting game of all time, and very beginner friendly as well. The game includes a decent sized single player mode (world tour) and a casual mode (battle hub). This is the best fighting game currently on the market, and the most beginner friendly fighting game as well. the combat is responsive.There are little input shortcuts to make CLASSIC inputs more viable on the competitive scene (whether on pad, stick, or hitbox) classic SF 6 button layout, classic moves are preserved,"MODERN" input added for newbiesm Soundtrack for specific fighters is top tier. If this is your first Street Fighter game or fighting game, you won't be disappointed or let down. CAPCOM really did a good job in getting this game to a point where it still calls to classic fans, but also invites new players. 10/10 loved it had so much fun.

One of the most polished fighting games in the market right now. Beginner friendly, amazing ranked system, top-notch netcode, a huge player base, and a lot of single player content with the world tour mode. The big downside though is the business model, with the character passes being extremely expensive. If you want to buy individual characters they only offer you packs of premium currency that have more than what you actually need to buy them. If you don't mind the DLCs the base game is completely recommended.

SF6 is a beefy package. You get a decent single player mode that plays a lot like Yakuza, a virtual chat room arcade in Battle Hub, arcade mode and full training suite. There's party mode (Extreme Matches) where you dodge bombs or fulfil challenges to win on points.

Capcom thought of the casual player and added Modern controls, which simplify special moves into a single input. Seems to work out for some players who find the classic controls too difficult.

The gameplay is fine, I prefer older SF games where people didn't drive rush at each other endlessly but it's still an interesting game to lab and try to understand.

There's definitely long periods of content drought and Capcom focuses too much on clothing for your avatar instead of costumes for the roster. The content comes from a battle pass every month. To Capcom's credit, if you beat a battle pass you get all your premium currency back so the next one is "free". If you keep playing regularly you'll always have more things to work towards. It's a shame most of it is garbage.

I had almost forgotten about fighting games. Over winter one of my kids got the Marvel vs Capcom collection for switch. The moment I heard the character selection music for MVC2, the memories of spending countless hours playing fighting games against my friends in the early 00s/late 90s came back. I was hooked again, and the kids and I started playing nearly daily. A couple months later I downloaded Street Fighter 6 to see what the newest release was like. This game is fantastic. Classic controls are classic, quarter circle forward and so on. Modern controls are really fun for people who just want to get into the thick of it. Dynamic controls make it so I can play with my littler kids and we can have a ton of fun. Watching a 5 year old smash on buttons and do flashy combos is a blast (and makes you really practice your punishes.) I was shocked to see that we've spent 140 hours in the games after a few months. I'm pretty sure there was a day that a kid left it on but I haven't spent 100+ hours on a game this quickly since diablo 3. 100% would recommend.

Game would be good if it wasn't monitized at every turn, including alternate base pallets, stages, music, etc. Capcom really shows just how greedy they are with this game. The base game itself outside of the story mode is barebones at best and lacks much when it comes to replayability.

A great entry point into the series if you've never played a SF game or even a fighting game in general. It's incredibly accessible and has loads of tutorials. The single player mode is okay. I wouldn't say its all that interesting or rewarding to play, but it is fun to guide your avatar through the wacky world and learn about the characters.

Learning how to play this game over the past 2 years (still learning) has been very fulfilling. Finally nailing the combos youve practiced in an online match is an amazing feeling. Double Perfecting an unga bunga Akuma will give you such a high that you'll wonder why you play anything else.

There is also an amazing community of people who want to help you learn if you know where to look. The pro players are fun to watch and the tournaments are very hype. 

My only issue is that the content roll-out is kind of slow for this game. For now they are only releasing 4 new characters a year and the costumes for the current characters are coming out at an even slower pace.

ITS FUN!
